mainTopic: A חזקה only counts with a טענה, and the cases of walls rebuilt by mistake on a neighbor's land.
overview: The amud first finishes an earlier topic. If a gift document does not say whether the giver wanted it public, do we worry that it was a concealed gift? רבינא says no, רב אשי says yes, and the הלכה follows רב אשי. Then a new משנה teaches that using land (חזקה) proves nothing unless the user also gives a reason (טענה) for how it became his, such as a sale or a gift. An heir does not need such a reason. The גמרא explains that the משנה is needed because we might have thought the court should suggest a 'lost document' claim for the holder (פתח פיך לאלם), and it teaches that the court does not. Next comes a story: רב ענן rebuilt his flood-damaged wall on his neighbor's land, and רב נחמן told him to move it back. רב נחמן rejected both of רב ענן's arguments. There is no instant חזקה, and the neighbor's help building the wall was a מחילה בטעות, a giving-up based on a mistake. A similar story about רב כהנא begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What about a gift document with no details?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to treat a gift document that does not say whether the gift was meant to be public or concealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law when the document is unspecified?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its earlier discussion about concealed gifts. It asks about the in-between case, where the document says nothing either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא dealt with gifts the giver wanted kept hidden, which are treated as weak or suspicious. A clear 'public' gift is fine and a clear 'hidden' gift is a problem. The question is which way to lean when nothing is said.

phrases.english: An unspecified one, what is its law?
phrases.notes: This means a gift document that doesn't say whether the giver wanted it public or kept hidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of concealed gifts by asking about the unspecified case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an unspecified gift document is treated as possibly concealed or as normal.

steps.title: רבינא and רב אשי disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says we do not worry that it was concealed. רב אשי says we do worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: we are not concerned. רב אשי said: we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question with opposite views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא assumes a normal gift unless we are told it was hidden. רב אשי holds that a document without details leaves room for suspicion, so we treat it with caution.

phrases.english: Ravina said: We are not concerned,
phrases.notes: He means we don't worry that it was a concealed gift.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with two opposing views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבינא: no concern of concealment. רב אשי: there is concern.

steps.title: The ruling: we are concerned
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב אשי: an unspecified gift document is treated with suspicion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the law is: we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the argument and rules like רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because we are concerned, an unspecified gift document does not get the full strength of a clearly public gift. This closes the discussion of gift documents before the new משנה begins.
steps.whatToRemember: An unspecified gift document is treated as possibly concealed. The הלכה follows רב אשי.

phrases.english: And the law is: We are concerned.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב אשי: we are concerned that an unspecified gift may be concealed.

steps.title: Using land without a claim proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a חזקה with no טענה is not a חזקה. Its example is someone who only says 'nobody ever objected.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Any possession that has no claim with it is not a valid possession. How so? The owner says to him, 'What are you doing on my property?' and he answers, 'No one ever said anything to me.' That is not a valid possession.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that years of using land prove nothing unless the user also explains how the land became his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה works as a sign that the holder probably bought the land and lost the paperwork. If the holder himself never claims he bought it, there is nothing for the חזקה to support. Saying 'nobody stopped me' is not a reason for owning land.

keyTerms.meaning: possession or use of land for the set time, which can establish ownership
a claim, an explanation of how one became owner

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the years of use are worthless in themselves. They only work when attached to a claim of purchase or gift; on their own they prove nothing.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Any possession that has no claim with it
is not a valid possession. How so?
He said to him:
phrases.notes: The first 'he' is the original owner, speaking to the person using the land.

phrases.english: "What are you doing in what is mine?"
And he said to him:
"Because no person ever said anything to me"
it is not a valid possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל חֲזָקָה שֶׁאֵין עִמָּהּ טַעֲנָה, אֵינָהּ חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה without a טענה of ownership is not a valid חזקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the whole סוגיא: a חזקה supports a claim but cannot replace one.

steps.title: Claims that make the possession valid
steps.stepSummary: If the holder says he bought the land or got it as a gift, from the owner or from the owner's father, the חזקה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'You sold it to me,' 'You gave it to me as a gift,' 'Your father sold it to me,' or 'Your father gave it to me as a gift,' that is a valid possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the positive side: examples of real claims that let the חזקה work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these is a real way land changes hands: sale or gift. It can come from the person now protesting or from his father. With such a claim, the years of use back it up, as if he had lost his document.

keyTerms.meaning: that you sold it to me

phrases.english: "Because you sold it to me";
"Because you gave it to me as a gift";
"Your father sold it to me";
"Your father gave it to me as a gift"
this is a valid possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting cases, where a proper טענה is present.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה with a claim of sale or gift, from the owner or his father, is valid.

steps.title: An heir needs no claim
steps.stepSummary: Someone who holds the land because he inherited it does not have to explain how his father got it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who comes because of inheritance does not need a claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception to its rule: an heir does not need to give a טענה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An heir could not know how his father acquired the land, so he cannot be expected to explain it. His claim is simply 'I inherited it,' and that is enough for the חזקה.
steps.whatToRemember: A חזקה needs a טענה such as sale or gift. The exception is an heir, who does not need to explain how his father got the land.

phrases.english: And one who comes because of inheritance
does not need a claim.
phrases.notes: He doesn't have to explain how his father got the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַבָּא מִשּׁוּם יְרוּשָּׁה אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ טַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the requirement of a טענה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An heir who holds land does not need to state how his ancestor acquired it.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה needs to teach that a חזקה without a claim is worthless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה, saying its rule seems too obvious to need saying. This sets up the גמרא's next move, which will explain what the משנה is really teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the holder gives no reason for owning the land, of course his use alone proves nothing. The גמרא assumes the משנה would not state something trivial, so a hidden point must be in it.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the opening rule of the משנה (step 4) needs to be stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a חזקה without a טענה is not a חזקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems so obvious that there is no need to state it, and a משנה does not teach the obvious.

steps.title: The court does not make up a lost-document claim for him
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed. Otherwise we might think the court should suggest to the holder that he had a document that got lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: maybe this man really bought the land and had a document that got lost. He only said 'nobody objected' because he thought that if he said 'I bought it,' they would tell him to show the document. So we should suggest to him: 'Maybe you had a document and lost it?' This would be a case of 'Open your mouth for the mute.' The משנה teaches us that we do not do this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 7. It explains what mistake the משנה is protecting us from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought the court should argue for the holder, the way it sometimes speaks up for someone who cannot speak for himself (פתח פיך לאלם). The משנה teaches that here the court does not make up a claim for him. If he does not say on his own that he bought the land, his חזקה is worthless.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces the mistaken idea the source comes to correct
A document, here a bill of sale
'Open your mouth for the mute': the court sometimes suggests a claim for a litigant
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: A חזקה needs the holder himself to say how he got the land. The court will not invent a 'lost document' story for him.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'Open your mouth for the mute' is the mistaken idea here. The משנה rejects using it in this case.

phrases.english: Lest you say:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי גַּבְרָא – מִיזְבָּן זְבִנָה לֵיהּ הַאי אַרְעָא,
phrases.english: This man really bought this land,
and he had a document, but it got lost;
and the reason he speaks this way is that he thought:
phrases.notes: 'This way' means only saying 'nobody ever objected,' as in Step 4.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמֵינָא מִיזְבָּן זְבִנָה לִי הַאי אַרְעָא,
phrases.english: If I say, 'He sold me this land,'
they will say to me: 'Show your document';
therefore, let us say to him:
Maybe you had a document and it got lost?
A case like this is one of 'Open your mouth for the mute';
so it teaches us that we do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 about why the משנה's rule is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reasonable mistaken idea (מהו דתימא) that the משנה comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court should suggest a lost-document claim for the holder, based on פתח פיך לאלם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court does not suggest it. A חזקה without his own טענה is worthless.

steps.title: A memory sign for the coming stories
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory word, ענב, before the next set of cases.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives a memory word to help learners remember the stories that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No law is taught here. It marks the start of a new section of cases about חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign that helps remember the order of the coming cases

phrases.english: (ענב is a memory sign)

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup line, not a true ruling
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Marks a move from the משנה's discussion to a new series of stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; a memory aid only.

steps.title: רב נחמן tells רב ענן to move his wall back
steps.stepSummary: After a flood, רב ענן rebuilt his boundary wall on his neighbor's land. רב נחמן told him to return it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A flood swept through רב ענן's land. He went and rebuilt the wall, but on his neighbor's land. He came before רב נחמן, who said to him: Go put it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רב נחמן rules that a wall rebuilt on someone else's land must be moved back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flood washed away the old boundary wall, and the new wall ended up past the real border. רב נחמן's ruling means that building the wall did not give רב ענן ownership of that strip.

keyTerms.meaning: A flood or breach of water
A wall, here the boundary wall

phrases.english: A flood swept through רב ענן's land.
phrases.notes: Literally 'a breach took his land.' The water knocked down the wall marking the border.

phrases.english: He went and rebuilt the wall
in his neighbor's land.
He came before רב נחמן,
who said to him: Go put it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the first story after the memory sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wall built on a neighbor's land must be moved back to the real border.

steps.title: רב ענן claims he already has a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן objects that he has already established a חזקה on the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I already established a חזקה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן pushes back against רב נחמן's ruling. He argues that the land is now his because of a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neighbor apparently saw the wall go up and did not protest. רב ענן reasons that taking possession this way already gave him a חזקה, so he should not have to move the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: I took possession; I established a חזקה

phrases.english: But I already established a חזקה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's order in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's order to move the wall back
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If building the wall created a חזקה, the land now belongs to רב ענן and he should not have to return it.

steps.title: No instant חזקה: the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that an immediate חזקה only works according to רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל, and the הלכה does not follow them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: According to whom are you speaking? Like רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל, who say that anything done in the owner's presence is a חזקה immediately? The הלכה is not like them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects רב ענן's claim. He explains that the opinion behind it is not the accepted הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ענן's claim only works if taking possession in front of the owner creates a חזקה right away, which is the view of רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל. Since the הלכה does not follow them, a fresh act of possession is not yet a חזקה. So the wall must go back.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Asks which opinion a claim relies on
In his presence, in front of the owner
The הלכה is not like them

steps.whatToRemember: Building on someone's land in front of him does not instantly make it yours. The הלכה rejects an immediate חזקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows in practice that a חזקה takes more than one act of taking possession, even when the owner sees it and stays quiet.

phrases.english: He said to him: According to whom?
Like רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל, who say:
Anything done in his presence is a חזקה immediately?
phrases.notes: 'His presence' means in front of the owner, here the neighbor who watched the wall go up.

phrases.english: The הלכה is not like them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ענן's objection in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the objection to a minority opinion that is not the הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Taking possession in front of the owner creates a חזקה right away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל, so there is no instant חזקה and the wall must be returned.

steps.title: The neighbor helped build the wall, so he gave up the land
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן argues that his neighbor gave up his claim to the land, because the neighbor came and helped build the wall in its new spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said to רב נחמן: But my neighbor gave up the land! He came and helped me build the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן pushes back on רב נחמן a second time. Even without a חזקה, he says, the neighbor himself gave up the land by helping build the wall there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first argument, the חזקה, was turned down in the previous step. Now he switches to a new reason: the neighbor's own actions. If the owner helped put the wall on his own land, it looks like he agreed to give that strip away.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave up his right (he waived it)
A wall, here the boundary wall between the fields

phrases.english: He said to him: But he gave it up!
phrases.notes: רב ענן is speaking to רב נחמן, and "he" is the neighbor who owned the land.

phrases.english: For he came and helped with the wall together with me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his חזקה claim was turned down in step 12, רב ענן offers a different reason to keep the land.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling (step 10) that רב ענן must give the land back
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the owner helped build the wall on his own land, he must have agreed to give that land up, so there is nothing to give back.

steps.title: It was a giving-up based on a mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the neighbor's help was a מחילה בטעות. The neighbor did not know the wall was on his land, just as רב ענן did not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: This is a giving-up made by mistake. You yourself, if you had known, would not have built it there. Just as you did not know, he did not know either.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains why the neighbor's help does not count as giving up the land: he did not know where the true boundary was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving something up only counts if the person knows what he is giving up. רב נחמן proves the neighbor did not know by pointing to רב ענן himself: רב ענן would never have built on someone else's land on purpose, so clearly nobody knew where the line was. A giving-up based on wrong information does not take effect, so the land still belongs to the neighbor.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving up a right by mistake, which does not count

steps.whatToRemember: Helping someone or keeping quiet is not a real מחילה if the person did not know the facts. A מחילה בטעות does not take effect, so רב ענן must return the land.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the neighbor lied or was tricked. Both men honestly did not know the true boundary, and that shared lack of knowledge is exactly why the giving-up does not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that a waiver only counts with knowledge, an idea that comes up often in דיני ממונות.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a giving-up made by mistake.

phrases.aramaic: אַתְּ גּוּפָךְ – אִי הֲוָה יָדְעַתְּ לָא עֲבַדְתְּ;
phrases.english: You yourself, if you had known, would not have done it;
phrases.notes: He means: if you had known this was your neighbor's land, you would not have built the wall there.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאַתְּ לָא הֲוָה יָדְעַתְּ,
phrases.english: just as you did not know,
he too did not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ענן's claim in step 13 that the neighbor gave up the land.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Takes away the force of the evidence: the act happened, but it was done without knowledge, so it has no legal effect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the neighbor helped build the wall on his own land, he agreed to give that land up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The neighbor did not know the wall was on his land, so his help was a מחילה בטעות and does not count. The land stays his.

steps.title: רב כהנא's wall is also rebuilt on someone else's land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new, similar story: a flood swept through רב כהנא's field, and he rebuilt his wall on land that was not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: A flood swept through רב כהנא's land. He went and rebuilt the wall on land that was not his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second story that looks just like רב ענן's case. It gives only the facts here, and the discussion of his case continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב ענן, רב כהנא lost his boundary wall to a flood and rebuilt it in the wrong place, on land that was not his. This is the next story after the memory word ענב from step 9. The גמרא will now discuss what happens in his case.

keyTerms.meaning: A flood or stream of water that breaks through

phrases.english: Rav Kahana: a flood swept through his land.
phrases.notes: The flood knocked down the wall that marked the line between his field and his neighbor's.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל הַדַּר גּוּדָא בְּאַרְעָא דְּלָא דִּידֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He went and rebuilt the wall on land that was not his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רב ענן's case, the גמרא opens another case, which has the same kind of facts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This step only sets out the facts: רב כהנא rebuilt his flood-damaged wall on land that was not his.
